full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.03.2009 of the High Court Division passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6908 of 2008 making the Rule absolute upon quashing the proceeding of Session Case No. 416 of 2007 of the Court of Sessions Judge, Rajshahi which arose out of C.R. Case No. 218 of 2007 of the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Rajshahi filed under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881. 

 2. The petitioner filed the above C.R. Case No. 218 of 2007 on the averments that the accused respondent No. 1 issued in his favour a cheque bearing No. 0823202 dated 15.04.2007 drawn on Rajshahi Markentile Bank Limited, Rajshahi for Tk.3,30,00,000/ towards repayment of his outstanding dues and thereafter the petitioner, on the same day, presented the said cheque in his bank but the same returned dishonoured on the ground of insufficient fund and he then by legal notice dated 24.04.2007 requested the respondent No. 1 for repayment of the said amount and though the respondent No. 1 received the said notice on 24.04.2007 but did not repay the same. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Rajshahi took cognizance of the offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and after receiving the summons the respondent No. 1 surrendered and obtained bail on 21.06.2007. The case record being transmitted to the Court of Sessions Judge, Rajshahi, Sessions Case No. 416 of 2007 was registered and then the learned Sessions Judge, by order dated 24.7.2007, took cognizance of the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and by order dated 08.08.2007 framed charge against the respondent No. 1 under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881. Thereafter receiving the case records from the Court of Sessions Judge Rajshahi, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rajshahi fixed the next dates on 27.01.2008 and then on 16.03.2008 and lastly on 12.05.2008 for trial of the above case but in the meantime the respondent No. 1 filed an application before the High Court Division under section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the grounds that legal notice was received by him on 24.04.2007 but the complaint petition, upon which the above C.R. Case No. 218 of 2007 was initiated, was filed on 23.5.2007, i.e before any cause of action arose for filing the above C.R. Case No.  218 of 2007. The High Court Division, after hearing, made the Rule absolute. 

 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the institution of the aforesaid C.R. Case before the expiry of 30 (thirty) days from the receipt of the legal notice by the accused respondent is nothing but a premature institution and before the High Court Division it was argued that if the cause of action matured during pendency of the proceedings, the defect of prematurity of the cause of action could be cured and inspite of that the High Court Division erroneously made the Rule absolute.
